Explicit rules, the same for every simulation, so they can be compared.
Points straight at the weak spot.
trading.fsExplain_sumVerdict_cons:
Each test's thresholds are conventions; a test narrowly failing changes the label.
All tests use the same history: none replaces paper or live trading.
It does not test everything (liquidity, broker rule changes, real execution).
trading.fsExplain_sumVolatility_what: The standard deviation of the performance index's daily returns, annualised with √365 (crypto trades every day). It says how much the strategy's capital swings, in %, over a typical year.
trading.fsExplain_sumVolatility_read: Compare it with the asset's own volatility (in 2.1, data quality): a strategy that is often out of the market should be well below it. For crypto, 20–40% is moderate and above 60% very choppy. What counts is the relation to return, which is the Sharpe: high volatility is only acceptable if the return pays for it.
trading.fsExplain_sumVolatility_pros:
A simple, standard risk measure, the basis of the Sharpe and of many sizing models.
Lets the strategy's risk be compared with the asset's.
trading.fsExplain_sumVolatility_cons:
Penalises up and down moves alike.
Does not capture extreme tails or the sequence of losses (see VaR, kurtosis and drawdown in 1.4).
Days without a position lower it, even though the risk while in the market is not smaller.
trading.fsExplain_sumWinRate_what: The % of trades that closed with positive net P&L (after fees and funding). Below, the payoff: the average win divided by the average loss.
trading.fsExplain_sumWinRate_read: Win rate only makes sense together with payoff: 35% wins with a payoff of 3 is profitable, 70% with a payoff of 0.3 loses. The break-even point is win rate = 1 ÷ (1 + payoff). Trend strategies tend to have a low win rate and high payoff; mean-reversion the opposite. See the R distribution in 4.5 and win rate by entry in 4.1.
trading.fsExplain_sumWinRate_pros:
Easy to grasp and tells how the strategy will feel day to day (many or few losses).
Together with payoff, it explains where the profit comes from.
trading.fsExplain_sumWinRate_cons:
Misleading on its own: a high win rate can hide rare but huge losses.
Trades with near-zero P&L (break-even after fees) count as losses.
With few trades it varies a lot by chance.
trading.fsExplain_sumWorstDay_what: The worst return of a single UTC day across the simulation, on the performance index (without deposits, open positions at the end-of-day price), with the best one below.
trading.fsExplain_sumWorstDay_read: Ask whether a day like that could be stomached with real money. Compare the worst day with max drawdown: if a good part of the maximum drop came in one day, risk is concentrated (gaps, liquidations, skipped stops). A best day far larger than the rest may mean the result depends on a single event (see concentration in the verdict).
trading.factsheetRulesInfo: Stop adjustments and scale-ins: how often they happened, how those trades ended and the result without each one.
trading.fsSetupNote: How often each setup armed and what came next
trading.fsSetupFootnote: Armed: met while disarmed. Renewed: met while armed, count restarted. Expired: candles ran out with no signal. Signalled: conditions met while armed; those signals go to the funnel.
trading.fsContextNote: Signals each account condition stopped and the result without it
trading.fsRuleFootnote: Each signal counts on the first failed condition. «Adds» = current return − return without the rule: positive, it helps.
trading.fsStopRulesNote: When each adjustment happened, trades that exited on its stop and the result without it
trading.fsStopRulesFootnote: Happened: the adjustment fired before the exit. Exited on it: closed on its stop. R on initial risk. «Adds» = current return − return without it.
trading.fsScaleInsNote: Scale-ins filled, those that didn't fit the capital and the result without each
trading.fsScaleInsFootnote: Reached: price (or conditions) got to the scale-in before the exit. Filled: added quantity (smaller: less than asked, for lack of capital). R on initial risk.
trading.fsScaleInsFootnoteSkipped: Some scale-ins didn't fit: the position already used all the capital (common with risk or «all» sizing). Use a smaller size.
trading.fsSchemesAddsNote: With risk sizing scale-ins may not fit: the column shows how many were left out
trading.fsOrderTypesNote: Limit and stop = level orders; the wait is in candles until filled
trading.fsVariantsNote: Same condition, only the order changes. Δ = return difference of the whole strategy
trading.fsExecutionNote: Open (default), previous close or 1st-minute average. The difference measures sensitivity to the entry price
trading.fsExecution_first_minute_avg: Average price of the first minute
trading.factsheetSampleInfo: Trades after the first {{pct}}% of the period, separately. Fitted to history, a strategy wins inside and loses outside.
trading.fsSampleDefault: No split set: uses the last {{pct}}%, like the score.
trading.fsSampleEquityNote: Right of the dashed line, the parameters never saw the data
trading.factsheetEntriesInfo: Per entry, in and out of sample. An entry that only wins in the first part shouldn't stay on.
trading.factsheetExitMatrixInfo: Each entry → exit pair. Cell colour is the average P&L.
trading.factsheetStopsInfo: How many stops, what they cost, how many reversed and the profit each exit leaves on the table.
trading.factsheetAfterInfo: What price did after each exit: take too short, stop too early, trailing giving back too much.
trading.factsheetDistributionsInfo: Result in R (multiples of initial risk), maximum adverse excursion and duration.
trading.factsheetCapitalInfo: Each entry's risk is picked from in-sample trades only; the «out» column is the one that counts.
trading.fsEntCard_flipsDetail: Positive in one part, negative in the other
trading.fsHelp_entBest: The entry with the highest P&L and its trades' average R
trading.fsHelp_entWorst: The entry with the lowest P&L and its trades' average R
trading.fsHelp_entLosing: Entries that ended with a negative P&L
trading.fsHelp_entFlips: Average R positive in one part and negative in the other. What only worked in one part may be luck.
trading.fsHelp_entWithoutWorst: Return of the strategy run without the worst entry, against the return with all
trading.fsEntFootnote: «Without this entry» = return with it off (the others get more free capital and positions).
trading.fsEntEquityNote: Cumulative P&L of each entry, in {{quote}}
trading.fsExitMixNote: % of each entry's trades by exit type
trading.fsStopCard_ofLossesDetail: The rest exit before the stop
trading.fsStopCard_extraDetail: Exit worse than the stop (gaps and slippage)
trading.fsHelp_stopStops: Trades that exited at the fixed stop loss (trailing and break-even count separately)
trading.fsHelp_stopOfLosses: Of the losing trades, the share that exited at the stop. The rest lost on another exit first.
trading.fsHelp_stopReversed: Stops where price reached that entry's take within 48 h. Many = stop too tight.
trading.fsHelp_stopExtra: How much worse than the stop level the exit was on average, in % of price: gaps and slippage
trading.fsHelp_stopTime: The average bars from the entry to the stop
trading.fsHelp_stopStreak: The longest run of consecutive stops, in exit order
trading.fsHelp_stopBreakEvens: Exited at the entry price after the stop moved there
trading.fsHelp_stopTakes: Trades that exited at the take profit
trading.fsReasonsFootnote: Left on the table = average MFE − average result, in % of price.
trading.fsStopsMonthNote: Bars = stops per month; line = average. Below, how often you took N stops in a row
trading.fsAfterNote_trailing_stop: If it keeps going your way, the trailing is tight
trading.fsAfterNone_take_profit: No trade exited at the take profit
trading.fsAfterNone_stop_loss: No trade exited at the stop loss
trading.fsAfterNone_trailing_stop: No trade exited at a trailing stop
trading.fsRDistNote: The peak at −1R is the stops. The right tail pays for the system
trading.fsRDistWithoutStop: {{count}} trades without a stop are left out (they have no R)
trading.fsRDistEmpty: No entry has a stop, so there's no R to show
trading.fsMaeNote: Winners that went far against you = stop too wide; losers that barely did = stop too tight
trading.fsScheme_doubleBest: Double the best, zero on the worst
trading.fsSchemesUnavailable_noStop: The schemes size by risk at the stop: every entry needs a stop loss
trading.fsSchemesUnavailable_version: The schemes only run on strategies with entries (new simulations)
trading.fsKellyTitle: Kelly and suggested size per entry
trading.fsKellyNote: In-sample only. ¼ Kelly is the usual pick; above 2% per trade rarely pays off
trading.fsCorrelationNote: Weekly P&L per entry. Low correlation = they diversify; high = the same bet
trading.fsMatrixNote: Trades · win rate per pair; colour is average P&L (total in the tooltip)
trading.fsJournalNote: Newest first; dates in UTC, like the candles
trading.factsheetAnatomyInfo: How much of the best moment (MFE) the exit takes, how long it takes to get there, the trade after a win or loss and whether the 2nd pyramid position pays.
trading.fsAnaCard_captureDetail: How much of the best moment the exit captures
trading.fsHelp_anaCapture: Of the maximum favourable move (MFE), the share the exit took: sum of the move to exit ÷ sum of MFEs
trading.fsHelp_anaPeak: Average bars from entry to the best price. Below, the bars trades stay open.
trading.fsHelp_anaAfterLoss: Trades where the last one to exit before entry lost: average R, win rate and count
trading.fsHelp_anaAfterWin: Trades where the last one to exit before entry won: average R, win rate and count
trading.fsHelp_anaSeparation: The first bar where eventual winners' average R leads losers' by more than 0.5R. Before that, they can't be told apart.
trading.fsHelp_anaSecond: Trades opened while another position of the same entry was open: average R, count and P&L
trading.fsPathTitle: Average trade path (in R) since entry
trading.fsPathNote: Average R at each bar after entry, for eventual winners and losers. Where they split, a time stop makes sense
trading.fsPathEmpty: No entry has a stop: without it there's no R to follow
trading.fsEfficiencyNote: MFE = the best the trade was; capture is the share the exit took
trading.fsEfficiencyFootnote: Capture = final P&L ÷ best unrealised P&L (trades with MFE > 0); negative = the group gives back more than it had.
trading.fsNextNote: The trade by the previous one. If the trade after a loss is worse, there's mechanical «tilt» (or the sizing rule)
trading.fsGroupsTitle: Pyramid, order type and order in the day
trading.fsGroupsNote: 2nd position of the same entry, market vs level, and 1st trade of the day vs the rest
trading.fsGroup_laterInDay: Next trades on the same day
trading.fsBuyHoldWithDeposits: With each deposit bought as it came in
trading.factsheetHoursInfo: Trades, stops and result by entry hour, Lisbon time. Stops count by the hour the trade opened.
trading.factsheetHoursInfoZone: Trades, stops and result by entry hour, {{zone}} time. Stops count by the hour the trade opened.
trading.factsheetHoursInfoUtc: Trades, stops and result by entry hour, in UTC. Stops count by the hour the trade opened.
trading.fsHourCard_noStops: No trade closed at the stop loss
trading.fsHelp_hourBusiest: The hour with the most trades opened and its share of the total
trading.fsHelp_hourStopsEntry: The entry hour with the most trades closed at the stop loss, whenever they closed
trading.fsHelp_hourStopsExit: The hour most stops were hit (by close time)
trading.fsHelp_hourBest: The entry hour with the highest net P&L and its win rate
trading.fsHelp_hourWorst: The entry hour with the lowest net P&L and the % closed at the stop loss
trading.fsHelp_hourEmpty: Hours with no entry (blocked times, or the signal never came)
trading.fsHourEntriesTitle: Entries per hour and per entry type
trading.fsHourEntriesNote: Trades opened each hour, stacked by entry
trading.fsHourStopsNote: Full bar = trades opened that hour that hit the stop loss; on top, the stop %
trading.fsHourPnlNote: Net result in {{unit}} of trades opened each hour
trading.fsHourTableNote: One row per hour, with the session and the entry that opened most
trading.factsheetExitHoursInfo: The hour trades closed: a 9am entry can be stopped at 3pm, at the US open.
trading.fsExitHoursTitle: Exits per hour and per exit type
trading.fsExitHoursNote: Trades closed each hour, stacked by exit reason
trading.fsExitHourStopsNote: Stops by exit hour. Spikes at opens are normal; overnight ones deserve a filter
trading.fsExitHourWinsTitle: Take profits and trailing hit per hour
trading.fsExitHourWinsNote: Winning exits by hour (take profit, trailing and positive break-even)
trading.fsExitHourTableTitle: Entry → exit hour: where each entry's stop lands
trading.fsExitHourTableNote: Per entry, the 3 hours with most stops and the hour with most winning exits
trading.fsExitHourTableFootnote: Average hours on a 24 h clock (11pm and 1am give midnight). 1st-hour stops = within 60 min of entry; % of the entry's stops.

trading.factsheetWeekdaysInfoZone: By entry day ({{zone}} time). Crypto trades at weekends on less volume; futures and CFDs close Friday night to Sunday night.
trading.factsheetWeekdaysInfoUtc: By entry day (UTC). Crypto trades at weekends on less volume; futures and CFDs close Friday night to Sunday night.
trading.fsHelp_weekdayBusiest: The day with most trades opened and the average per day (÷ days of that kind in the period)
trading.fsHelp_weekdayStops: The day with the highest % of trades closed at the stop loss
trading.fsHelp_weekdayBest: The entry day with the highest net P&L and its average R
trading.fsHelp_weekdayWorst: The entry day with the lowest net P&L and its average R
trading.fsHelp_weekdayWeek: Net P&L of trades opened Monday to Friday, with win rate and % at the stop loss
trading.fsHelp_weekdayWeekend: Net P&L of trades opened at the weekend, with win rate and % at the stop loss
trading.fsWeekdayEntriesTitle: Entries per day and per entry type
trading.fsWeekdayEntriesNote: Trades opened on each day of the week
trading.fsWeekdayStopsTitle: Stops per day: entry time vs exit time
trading.fsWeekdayStopsNote: Dark = stops of trades opened that day; light = stops hit that day
trading.fsWeekdayPnlTitle: P&L per day of the week
